headline: Dry, foggy, cool days ahead, then a wetter, windier pattern returns next week.
summary: A ridge of high pressure, a zone of sinking, dry air, settles over Western Washington tonight and holds through Friday. Expect cool mornings, patchy fog, possibly freezing in the South Sound early Friday, and highs in the 40s to low 50s. The ridge breaks down Saturday, bringing light showers Saturday night into Sunday and little new snow in the mountains. Next week turns windier: a warm front arrives Monday and a cold front Tuesday, with a strong low pressure system well offshore. Expect strong coastal winds, breezy conditions inland, and possible coastal flooding as high tides coincide with the wind. Another system may arrive Wednesday night into Thanksgiving, but its track is uncertain.
